question: The temperature at which air becomes saturated is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is **"dew point".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The temperature at which air becomes saturated is known as the dew point.
 
• When the temperature is below the freezing point of water, the dew point is called the **frost point.**
 
• The more the dew point, the more will be the amount of moisture in the air.
 
• **If the dew point is less than or equal to 55**- dry and comfortable environment.
 
• **If it is between 55 and 65**, it becomes sticky.
 
• **Greater than or equal to 65**- lots of moisture in the air.
 
• The dew point is affected by humidity- more the moisture in the air, the higher the dew point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ice point -** This is the freezing point of pure water.** At 0° celsius,** the water and ice coexist in equilibrium at** 1 atmospheric pressure.**
 
• **Humidity point -** It is the concentration of water vapors present in the air. It indicates the likelihood of dew or fog.
 
 
• The higher the humidity, the wetter it feels outside.
 
 
 
• **Water point - **It means a source of water that can be a tap, well or borewell, etc.
